articles.title: India and Pakistan Agree to Immediate Ceasefire Amid Rising Tensions
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: India and Pakistan have agreed to an immediate ceasefire following days of heightened military tensions. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri confirmed that Pakistan’s Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) contacted his Indian counterpart at 15:35 hours today.

body.html:
India and Pakistan have agreed to an immediate ceasefire following days of heightened military tensions.

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri confirmed that Pakistan’s Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) contacted his Indian counterpart at 15:35 hours today. Both sides agreed to halt all firing and military operations—on land, air, and sea—starting from 17:00 IST.

The DGMOs are scheduled to hold further talks on May 12 at 12:00 hours.

articles.title: Fake AI Video of EAM Jaishankar Circulating Online, Says PIB Fact Check
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A doctored AI-generated video showing External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar allegedly apologizing—circulated with a fake Punjabi accent—has surfaced online as part of a false propaganda campaign.

body.html:
A doctored AI-generated video showing External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar allegedly apologizing—circulated with a fake Punjabi accent—has surfaced online as part of a false propaganda campaign.

PIB Fact Check has confirmed the video is fake and AI-generated, urging the public to stay alert and not fall for misinformation.

articles.title: India Dismisses Pakistan’s False Claims of Military Strikes: IAF
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: During a press briefing on Operation Sindoor, Wing Commander Vyomika Singh strongly rejected Pakistan’s ongoing misinformation campaign, which falsely claims the destruction of Indian military assets, including S-400 systems at Adampur, airfields at Suratgarh and Sirsa, the BrahMos base...

body.html:
During a press briefing on Operation Sindoor, Wing Commander Vyomika Singh strongly rejected Pakistan’s ongoing misinformation campaign, which falsely claims the destruction of Indian military assets, including S-400 systems at Adampur, airfields at Suratgarh and Sirsa, the BrahMos base at Nagrota, RT gun positions at Dehrangyari, and the Chandigarh Forward Ammunition Depot.

“These are baseless narratives being spread on social media. India unequivocally rejects them,” said Singh.
